# 1.02
Source: written
Write a function `odd::is_odd(int n)` that returns true when n is odd.
Limits: -1000 ≤ n ≤ 1000.
## Solution
```cpp
#pragma once

namespace odd {

//: Write a function that returns whether the test holds.
bool is_odd(int n)
{
    return [[n % 2 != 0]];
}

}  // namespace odd
```
## Slow
```cpp
#pragma once

namespace odd {

bool is_odd(int n)
{
    bool odd {false};
    for (int i {0}; i < (n < 0 ? -n : n); ++i) {
        odd = !odd;
    }
    return odd;
}

}  // namespace odd
```
## Tests
```cpp
TEST_CASE("three") { REQUIRE(odd::is_odd(3)); }
TEST_CASE("minus_four") { REQUIRE_FALSE(odd::is_odd(-4)); }
TEST_CASE("zero") { REQUIRE(odd::is_odd(0) == false); }
```
